summary:
Texas restricts trans people's use of sex-separated facilities under the Women's Privacy Act (SB 8), signed by Governor Greg Abbott on 22 September 2025 and effective 4 December 2025. Restrooms must match the sex recorded on a person's birth certificate, and the law reaches public schools, universities, prisons and Texas government buildings. Facilities face a $25,000 fine for a first violation and $125,000 for subsequent violations. The companion gender-placements statute reaches prisons only as to restroom use; it does not govern cell assignment or the housing placement of trans prisoners.

Enforcement began within days of the effective date. On 6 December 2025 Department of Public Safety troopers checked identification at women's restrooms outside the state Capitol in Austin, and trans women holding female ID markers were admitted. Protests followed at the Capitol, the Austin City Council moved to circumvent the law's intent, and opponents warned that unclear guidelines produce uneven and invasive enforcement.

On 27 April 2026 Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a second complaint that escalated the state investigation of Austin Independent School District over its bathroom policy, with a renewed records demand after a tip-line complaint. It was the first state enforcement inquiry into a school district under the bathroom law.

A national legal risk assessment dated July 2026 places Texas in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier for adult trans travellers, alongside Florida, Idaho and Kansas. States in that assessment are graded law by law across care bans, bathroom bans and enforcement posture using a five-year legislation-tracking methodology.

House Bill 229, the Women's Bill of Rights, passed in May 2025, signed in June 2025 and effective September 2025, defines female as a person who can biologically produce ova and male as one who can biologically fertilize ova, requires people with disorders of sex development to select one binary gender with no third-gender recognition, and applies across all state statutes, regulations and laws using gendered terms. The statute explicitly bans any change of sex on Texas driver's licences and birth certificates. Before it took effect, changing the gender indicator on a birth certificate required a court order, with judicial discretion often referencing WPATH Standards of Care and a narrative statement from a doctor or therapist that the change was appropriate and in the person's best interest; on 30 January 2025 Governor Abbott separately directed state agencies to recognise only two genders.

Gender-affirming care for minors has been banned in Texas since Senate Bill 14, signed in June 2023, which followed a February 2022 attorney general opinion classifying such care as child abuse.

Texas has no statewide law barring discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations or insurance as of 2021, although Texas courts recognised federal employment protections under Bostock v. Clayton County in March 2021 and several cities prohibit such discrimination. The state hate-crime statute enhances penalties for crimes motivated by sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity, and prosecutions under it are rare.

Custody carries documented harm. Vanessa Lynn Gibson, a transgender woman incarcerated by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice and diagnosed with gender dysphoria, was denied gender-confirmation surgery because the agency's official treatment policy excluded the procedure. In Gibson v. Collier the federal district court denied the state's immunity defences but ruled against her Eighth Amendment claim, and the Fifth Circuit affirmed dismissal on the ground that refusing the surgery was a permissible medical choice under Kosilek, with Judge Barksdale dissenting on summary-judgement procedure.

Same-sex marriage has been licensed in Texas since Obergefell v. Hodges on 26 June 2015, and the 2022 federal Respect for Marriage Act requires Texas to recognise lawfully performed out-of-state same-sex marriages without obligating the state to issue them. Texas has no statewide recognition of domestic partnerships for same-sex or opposite-sex couples, though Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio provide health insurance to domestic partners of city workers, and an April 2013 attorney general opinion held that the state constitution bars political-subdivision benefits based on domestic-partnership status.
tangentialFactors:
Texas shares the top 'Do Not Travel' tier with Florida, Idaho and Kansas in the July 2026 assessment. The grading is law by law across care bans, bathroom bans and enforcement posture rather than a tally of incidents, so the tier reflects statutory and enforcement conditions.

Opponents of the women's privacy statute warn that unclear guidelines produce uneven and invasive enforcement. The two documented enforcement episodes in this inventory are the identification checks outside the state Capitol on 6 December 2025 and the escalated complaint against Austin Independent School District on 27 April 2026; no later instance is documented.

Legislative activity has been sustained. Around fifty bills were filed in early January 2023 to criminalise youth gender-affirming care, reduce adult access, bar sex-marker changes for minors and further restrict sports participation. A prefiled November 2022 bill would expand the definition of sexually oriented businesses to reach any performance where a performer uses clothing, makeup or other markers to exhibit gender variance from birth-assigned sex while singing, lip-syncing, dancing or otherwise performing, which would capture transgender performers in any role as well as cisgender portrayals of diverse or ambiguous genders, and would criminalise minors' attendance at drag shows.
localsOnly:
Senate Bill 14, signed June 2023, effectively bans gender-affirming care for minors. It followed a February 2022 attorney general opinion classifying such care as child abuse and governor directives ordering the Department of Family and Protective Services to investigate parents who facilitate it and imposing criminal penalties for a knowing failure to report. Five district attorneys refused to follow the directives, and a March 2022 temporary injunction blocked them; the Third Court of Appeals reinstated the injunction after an ACLU and Lambda Legal suit on behalf of providers including Dr. Megan Mooney and a family with a 16-year-old transgender girl on puberty blockers. Investigative supervisor testimony stated that trans-child cases faced different rules, with mandatory investigation regardless of evidence and a prohibition on discussing them by email or text. Earlier legislative efforts included 2021 House Bill 1399 and Senate Bill 1311, passed 18-13, to revoke the licences of doctors providing blockers to minors, while House Bill 1106 excludes a parent's refusal to affirm a child's gender identity or sexual orientation from the child-abuse definition.

The Parents' Bill of Rights, enacted June 2025, bars school employees from teaching or discussing gender identity, bans LGBT-related student organisations, mandates deadnaming and misgendering of trans students and expands parental authority over schools.

As of 2021 no state law bars employment, housing, public-accommodations or insurance discrimination based on gender identity, though Texas courts recognised federal employment protections in March 2021. Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, Plano and San Antonio prohibit gender-identity discrimination in private and public employment, housing and public accommodations, with narrower city-employment or public-accommodation protections in Denton, El Paso, Arlington, Brownsville, Corpus Christi, Houston, Irving, Lubbock, Mesquite and Waco. A law effective 1 September 2025 explicitly listing banned DEI school and certain workplace programmes for sexual orientation is in effect and under court challenge, and voters passed a constitutional parental-rights amendment in November 2025.

Any adult may adopt regardless of sexual orientation, and legally married same-sex couples can adopt jointly and obtain supplemental birth certificates listing both parents. Lesbian couples may access IVF and assisted insemination, though health-plan IVF coverage requiring fertilisation only with the spouse's sperm restricts access, and even federally funded adoption agencies may discriminate on religious beliefs.

Domestic-partner benefits are local matters: Dallas County paid $300 per month cash subsidies in October 2012, Travis, El Paso and Bexar Counties allow partner participation, and Pflugerville ISD allows inclusion at full worker cost. A November 2013 voter-approved city measure in Houston was interpreted to require spousal benefits for legally married same-sex couples, and an April 2013 attorney general opinion held the constitution bars political-subdivision benefits based on domestic-partnership status.

Same-sex sexual activity was decriminalised by Lawrence v. Texas in June 2003, but as of 2023 Texas remains one of three states retaining a dormant same-sex-only sodomy statute termed deviate sexual intercourse; a 2025 House-passed repeal failed in the Senate. Texas retains a same-sex-exclusionary Romeo-and-Juliet affirmative defence allowing a defence only if the actor is not more than three years older than a child under 17 or is a spouse and not of the child's same sex, with no published constitutional challenge since Obergefell.

Other resident-facing measures include June 2019 SB 1978 barring adverse government action for supporting religious organisations that may refuse LGBTQ service, an October 2020 internal policy permitting social-worker discrimination against LGBT clients, the February 2022 removal of The Trevor Project from state suicide-prevention resources, and a rule effective in 2025 under which judges refusing same-sex weddings on religious grounds face no punishment.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory contains no trans-specific violence or killing figures for Texas, so no comparison against the state's general homicide rate can be drawn from these sources.

Guidance accompanying the women's privacy statute remains unclear in these sources; opponents warn of uneven enforcement, and no identification-check episode later than 6 December 2025 is documented here.

The Austin Independent School District investigation was escalated on 27 April 2026, and no outcome is sourced.

The prefiled November 2022 bill on gender-variant performance has no documented status after pre-filing, and the court challenge to the law effective 1 September 2025 has no documented outcome in these sources.

Whether existing driver's licences or birth certificates carrying a changed gender marker can be renewed or amended after the September 2025 definition act is not sourced here.

The July 2026 risk assessment's tiering has no later update in this inventory.
